children: Shares of water control and measurement company Badger Meter
jumped 4.2% in the afternoon session after Northcoast analyst Ryan Connors upgraded the stock to Buy.

An upgrade to a Buy rating indicates that an analyst expects the equity to outperform over a given investment horizon. Brokerage firms and research analysts issue upgrades when their evaluation of a company's prospects or valuation becomes more favorable. Such rating adjustments frequently draw interest from institutional and retail market participants, leading to increased buying activity and upward pressure on the share price. The positive change in recommendation from Northcoast contributed to the gains during the trading session.
The shares were trading at $133.13, up 4.3% from the previous close.
What Is The Market Telling Us

Badger Meter’s shares are somewhat volatile and have had 12 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 5 months ago when the stock dropped 18.9% on the news that the company reported underwhelming first quarter results: sales, adjusted operating income and earnings per share fell short of Wall Street's estimates. Management attributed the weakness to "variability in project timing," essentially arguing that while the demand exists, the actual installation and billing of large-scale municipal projects shifted out of the first quarter. While the company expressed optimism for a "back-half weighted" 2026 and announced a strategic $100 million acquisition of UDlive to bolster its sewer-monitoring tech, investors are currently penalizing the stock for the near-term execution gap.

Badger Meter is down 24.5% since the beginning of the year, and at $133.13 per share, it is trading 29.1% below its 52-week high of $187.87 from November 2025. Despite the year-to-date decline, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Badger Meter’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,324.
